headline: Default shared-workspace and server-side tool execution create medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; compliance risk is low.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and act on filesystem content, and Dify exposes uploaded knowledge-base files plus agent/workflow tool wiring. That creates a plausible default path where Dify-produced content is consumed by AutoGPT as instructions or context. No provenance or isolation mechanism is documented in either profile, so the interaction is not safely blocked.
conditions: IF Dify outputs are copied into AutoGPT prompts or files without provenance filtering
IF both agents share a writable workspace or synced folder
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct directories
Add a manual review step before AutoGPT ingests Dify output
Prefix all Dify outputs with non-executable delimiters
Disable automatic file pickup between the agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and parser hardening

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify handles model provider API keys, tool credentials, knowledge-base files, and conversation logs, while AutoGPT has filesystem access and allowlisted network egress. If the pair shares files or workspace state, sensitive Dify content can be read by AutoGPT and then sent onward through its network path. The profiles do not show a blocking isolation boundary.
conditions: IF Dify conversation logs or uploaded files are placed in a directory AutoGPT can read
IF AutoGPT is allowed to transmit retrieved content through its allowlisted egress
mitigations: Store secrets and logs outside any shared folder
Restrict AutoGPT to a read-only, empty workspace
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately after testing
Review Dify uploads for secrets before sharing
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can execute shell commands and spawn subprocesses, and Dify can execute server-side Python code in a sandbox container while also writing files. Even without git modification, both can mutate shared resources if pointed at the same workspace, so write conflicts are plausible in default orchestration. The profiles do not document locking or coordination.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory
IF Dify code tools and AutoGPT shell steps target the same mutable files
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Run one agent at a time on shared artifacts
Make shared files read-only during the other agent's run
Check for file locks before writes
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination or locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an agent/workflow platform that can wire tools into agent flows, and AutoGPT is autonomous enough to generate outputs that Dify may treat as upstream context. If Dify forwards AutoGPT output without verification, errors can cascade into downstream tool actions or workflow decisions. No verification gate is documented in either profile.
conditions: IF Dify uses AutoGPT output as authoritative workflow input
IF downstream Dify tools act on that output without human or rule-based verification
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before actions
Require schema validation on AutoGPT outputs
Compare outputs against a second source
Limit downstream tools to read-only mode
requires-engineering: add confidence gating and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but Dify explicitly touches conversation logs, knowledge-base content, and provider API keys, while AutoGPT's profile does not show regulated-data handling or residency constraints. A compliance mismatch is possible only if regulated data is routed into Dify and then shared onward; the other agent is not independently implicated by the profiles.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Dify conversation logs or knowledge-base files
IF that data is then exported into AutoGPT or external model providers
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared prompts
Pseudonymize sensitive fields before ingestion
Review retention settings in Dify
Keep AutoGPT away from regulated datasets
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
